title: The neural architecture of social threat: A meta-analytic comparison of indirect and direct social threat
title_zh: 社会威胁的神经架构：间接与直接社会威胁的荟萃分析比较
abstract: Indirect and Direct Social Threat (IST and DST) are related but partially distinct forms of interpersonal adversity defined along two dimensions: threat perception, the explicitness and salience of harm, and behavioural reciprocity, the extent of bidirectional contingency and response opportunity. IST involves ambiguous or socially devaluing contexts with limited reciprocity, whereas DST entails overt hostility, clear antagonism, and reciprocal engagement. This distinction shows conceptual parallels with findings from rodent models of social interaction. We tested this framework using a coordinate-based Activation Likelihood Estimation (ALE) meta-analysis of human neuroimaging studies comprising 28 IST contrasts (N = 1081) and 28 DST contrasts (N = 855), with cluster-level family-wise error correction (p<.05). Findings were interpreted alongside passive and agonistic animal paradigms. Conjunction analysis identified shared spatial convergence in the left anterior insula (AI) extending into the inferior frontal gyrus (IFG), consistent with salience-detection and regulatory processes. ALE contrast analysis showed stronger convergence for DST than IST in the right AI, bilateral claustrum, and anterior and mid-cingulate cortices, regions implicated in motivational salience and action preparation; no clusters emerged for IST relative to DST. Predicted IST-specific convergence in the temporoparietal junction and posterior cingulate cortex, and DST-related convergence in the amygdala and ventral striatum, were not observed. This pattern is conceptually consistent with animal evidence associating reciprocal threat with defensive readiness and action selection. Overall, findings partially support the framework: threat perception and behavioural reciprocity may help organize neural responses to social threat, while correspondence with passive-agonistic animal models remains provisional.
abstract_zh: 间接社会威胁（IST）与直接社会威胁（DST）是相关但部分不同的两种人际逆境形式，按两个维度定义：威胁感知（伤害的明确性和显著性）以及行为互惠（双向依赖和回应机会的程度）。IST 涉及含糊或社会贬低的情境，互惠有限；DST 则涉及公开敌意、明确对抗和相互参与。该区分与啮齿类动物社会互动模型的发现在概念上相似。我们使用基于坐标的激活可能性估计（ALE）荟萃分析，对包含 28 个 IST 对比（N=1081）和 28 个 DST 对比（N=855）的人体神经影像研究进行检验，并采用聚类层面家族错误校正（p<.05）。结果与被动与攻击性动物范式一起解释。联合分析显示左前岛叶（AI）延伸至下额叶回（IFG）的空间共聚，符合显著性检测和调节过程。ALE 对比分析显示 DST 在右 AI、双侧 claustrum 以及前中扣带皮层的共聚更强，涉及动机显著性和行动准备；IST 相对 DST 未出现任何聚类。预测的 IST 特异性共聚在颞顶交界区和后扣带皮层，以及 DST 相关共聚在杏仁核和腹侧纹状体的观察未出现。该模式在概念上与动物证据一致，即相互威胁与防御准备和行动选择相关。总体而言，结果部分支持该框架：威胁感知和行为互惠可能有助于组织对社会威胁的神经反应，而与被动-攻击性动物模型的对应仍属初步。
